title: Curly braces are reserved for attribute syntax
message: Curly braces are reserved for attribute syntax in Quarto markdown. To write literal braces, escape them as `\{...\}`. If you meant to attach an attribute, use `.class` / `#id` / `key="value"` syntax, e.g. `[text]{.class}`.

cases.name: prose
cases.description: Bare brace run in prose (the strand's verbatim example; REST API docs write path parameters like {guid} constantly).
cases.content: the request returns the task {guid} immediately.

cases.name: link-text
cases.description: Brace run inside link text; fails at a different LR state than the bare-paragraph form. (Image alt text and bracketed span text reduce to this same state.)

cases.name: emphasis-star
cases.description: Brace run inside star emphasis; the LR state follows the innermost inline container, so `*...*` needs its own case (this is also the state reached by braces nested any depth inside emphasis).

cases.name: emphasis-underscore
cases.description: Brace run inside underscore emphasis; a different LR state from the star spelling.

cases.name: strong-star
cases.description: Brace run inside star strong emphasis.

cases.name: strong-underscore
cases.description: Brace run inside underscore strong emphasis; a different LR state from the star spelling.

cases.name: strikeout
cases.description: Brace run inside a strikeout span.

cases.name: superscript
cases.description: Brace run inside a superscript span.

cases.name: subscript
cases.description: Brace run inside a subscript span.

cases.name: double-quote
cases.description: Brace run inside a double-quoted span; smart quotes wrap their content in their own inline container.

cases.name: single-quote
cases.description: Brace run inside a single-quoted span; a different LR state from the double-quoted spelling.

cases.name: inline-note
cases.description: Brace run inside an inline footnote.

cases.name: editorial-span
cases.description: Brace run inside an editorial span. The four editorial spellings ([!! ...], [-- ...], [++ ...], [>> ...]) share one LR state, so one case covers all four.

cases.name: table-header-cell
cases.description: Brace run in a pipe-table header cell. Table cells are NOT covered by the paragraph case: `pipe_table_cell` is built on `_line_with_maybe_spaces`, a sibling of the `_inlines` every other container wraps, so it reaches its own LR states -- one for header cells, one for body cells.

cases.name: table-body-cell
cases.description: Brace run in a pipe-table body cell; a different LR state from the header cell. Any row or column of the body reduces to this one state.
